chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Salih ibn al-Sindi, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Isa al-Farra, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Four [things] are not permissible in four [acts of worship]: Betrayal (al-khiyanah), Booty/Plunder (al-ghulul), Theft (al-sariqah), and Usury/Interest (al-riba). These four are not permissible in Hajj, nor Umrah, nor Jihad, nor Charity (Sadaqah).

key_terms.الْغُلُولُ: Booty or excess taken secretly from war spoils
key_terms.جِهَادٌ: Striving or warfare in the path of God

ai.seo_question: What types of earnings invalidate acts of worship like Hajj and Jihad according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes that the validity of major acts of worship—Hajj, Umrah, Jihad, and Sadaqah—is contingent upon the purity of the wealth used, specifically excluding earnings tainted by betrayal (al-Khiyanah), plunder (al-Ghulul), theft, and usury (al-Riba). This hadith underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that spiritual acceptance is intrinsically linked to financial integrity, rendering these acts spiritually void if funded by illicit gains. It highlights the comprehensive nature of 'Ghulul' in Shia fiqh, extending beyond military booty to include any misappropriated wealth.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Salih Bin Al Sandy, from Ja’far Bin Basheer, from isa Al Farra, from Aban Bin Usman, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Four

would not be allowed (into Paradise and) regarding (those) four – the betrayal, and the excessiveness, and the theft, and the usury, these are not allowed during Hajj, nor Umrah, nor Jihaad, nor charity’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Salih ibn al-Sindiy from Ja’far ibn Bashir from ‘Isa al-Farra’ from Aban ibn ‘Uthman who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Four things are not lawful in four issues: treachery, excessiveness, theft and unlawful interest are not lawful in al-Hajj, al-‘Umrah, Jihad and charity.’”
